newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Kyrgyzstan creates new state oil and gas company.
newsitem.headline: Kyrgyzstan creates new state oil and gas company.

text.p: Kyrgyzstan has combined three state-owned oil and gas trading and refining enterprises into one company, a government official said on Monday.

Batyr Davlesov, a senior economic advisor to President Askar Akayev, told a news conference in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek that the new enterprise would comprise Kyrgyzgaz (gas), Chuigazmunaizat (oil and gas trade and refining) and the state-owned joint-stock company Kyrgyzmunaizat (oil trade and refining).
The new enterprise, which will trade and refine oil products, will keep the name Kyrgyzmunaizat.
The concern's new director, Shakhlar Dzhaisanbayev, said the new enterprise had been formed to streamline the state-owned enterprises to make them more competitive and cut losses.
Dzhaisanbayev said the new company on Monday had already lowered its price for petrol to 3.60 soms per litre from 4.20 soms per litre. ($1 = 17.17 soms)
